content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** Section 28.1 already gives us our preferred New York governing law, and no arbitration provision exists anywhere in the Agreement, so this is not walk-away territory. The single defect is in 28.2: the "exclusive jurisdiction" of the New York County courts is contradicted by the retained carve-out permitting either Party to seek temporary injunctive relief "in another court with jurisdiction." Because the fallback (Delaware/California/England and Wales) is inapplicable to a New York bargain, the clause must meet the preferred checklist, and the exclusivity element fails while that carve-out survives.

**Redline:** one surgical deletion of the carve-out sentence in p0116 — New York law, the CISG exclusion, the personal-jurisdiction submission, and the 28.3 pre-filing meet-and-confer process are all preserved verbatim.
